1.explanation: Both files are responsible for feeding Storybook Docs the metadata it needs to build API tables. UIShell.mdx currently imports and renders <Props /> with no <Meta> definition or `of` target, so the docs addon doesn’t know which component to inspect and falls back to “undefined.” The companion UIShell.stories.js also needs to export proper default metadata (title, component, subcomponents) so that <Props of={…}> can resolve each UIShell subcomponent. Updating UIShell.mdx to include a <Meta> block and/or explicit <Props of={Header}> (and likewise for the other subcomponents), and ensuring UIShell.stories.js has the correct CSF default export, will restore the autogenerated prop tables.
1.bug_scenario: When you open the UIShell section of our production Storybook (for example “Fixed SideNav” under the UIShell group), the “Component API” panel shows a tab labeled “undefined” alongside tabs for “Content,” “Header,” “HeaderMenuButton,” etc., and inside each it says “No inputs found for this component.” In other words, our MDX/docs stage isn’t picking up any of the UIShell components’ prop definitions and is defaulting to an undefined module.

2.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/UIShell/UIShell.mdx
   • This MDX page only imports and renders `<Props />` without ever defining a `<Meta>` or telling it which component to document. Storybook defaults to the story’s primary component metadata, and because none has been specified in the MDX, the table comes back empty and the default tab shows “undefined.”

2. packages/react/src/components/UIShell/UIShell.stories.js
   • The default export for this story file provides a `docs.page` override but does not supply a `component` field (e.g. `component: Header`). Without a `component` in the meta, `<Props />` has nothing to read for its “primary” tab.

3. packages/react/src/components/UIShell/index.js
   • Although this file re-exports every sub-component in the UIShell package, it does not export a single `UIShell` component or default export. Storybook’s autodocs assume a primary exported component; here the lack of a default or dedicated `UIShell` export causes the first tab to resolve to `undefined`.

By adding a `<Meta component={Header} />` (or whichever is intended) to the MDX, or by supplying a `component` in the .stories.js meta, and/or by exporting a dedicated `UIShell` component in `index.js`, you give Storybook’s docs engine something concrete to pick up, which will restore the missing prop tables.
2.bug_scenario: When you navigate to the production Storybook page for `UIShell` (for example “Fixed SideNav” under the UI Shell section), the “Component API” pane never actually shows any prop tables. Instead you see a tab labeled “undefined” alongside tabs for each sub-component (Content, Header, HeaderMenuButton, etc.) and a message “No inputs found for this component.” In other words, Storybook’s `<Props />` helper can’t resolve a primary component to document, so it never outputs the usual prop tables.
